All STEREO-A-informed variants agree on an SIR compression pulse hitting the comet around Dec 3.6–4.9, with the real uncertainty being the pulse's arrival timing (±0.3 d) rather than its amplitude—OSSE twin experiments will test how well the DA pins this down. I'm now adding an X-ray light-curve comparison panel purely for validation context, not for tuning.

{
  "command": "cd /mnt/c/Users/cabot/OneDrive/Documents/Research/Cambridge/X3I/mhd_llm/claude/src/py && cat >> product_timeseries.py <<'EOF'


def lightcurve_compare(members, out):
    lc = pd.read_csv(PRE / "lightcurve.tsv", sep="\t")
    lc["utc"] = pd.to_datetime(lc.midpoint_utc)
    g = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data/xmm/pn_gti.csv")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.5))
    tg = np.arange(I.tsec("2025-12-03T06:00"), I.tsec("2025-12-05T00:00"), 900.0)
    utc = I.T_REF + pd.to_timedelta(tg, unit="s")
    rows = {}
    for nm, m in members.items():
        f = np.interp(tg, m.t, m.flux_rel)
        fr = []
        for r in lc.itertuples():
            gg = g[g.frame == r.frame]
            ts = np.concatenate([np.linspace(I.tsec(a), I.tsec(b), 20) for a, b in zip(gg.start_utc, gg.stop_utc)])
            fr.append(np.mean(np.interp(ts, m.t, m.flux_rel)))
        fr = np.asarray(fr)
        rows[nm] = {"frame_flux": fr.tolist(), "corr_with_rate": float(np.corrcoef(fr, lc.rate_ct_s)[0, 1]), "frame_dynamic_range": float(fr.max() / fr.min())}
        ax.plot(utc, f / np.median(fr), lw=1, alpha=0.8, label=f"{nm} (r={rows[nm]['corr_with_rate']:.2f})")
    ax.errorbar(lc.utc, lc.rate_ct_s / lc.rate_ct_s.median(), yerr=lc.error_ct_s / lc.rate_ct_s.median(), fmt="ks", ms=4, label="EPIC-pn 0.2-1 keV rate (preprint)")
    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.set_ylabel("normalized to median over PN frames")
    ax.axvspan(pd.Timestamp(I.OBS_ALL[0]), pd.Timestamp(I.OBS_ALL[1]), color="orange", alpha=0.15)
    ax.legend(fontsize=6)
    ax.set_title("Model comet-frame proton flux vs PN light curve (validation context only; not used for tuning)", fontsize=9)
    fig.autofmt_xdate()
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out, dpi=140)
    plt.close(fig)
    Path(out).with_suffix(".json").write_text(json.dumps({"rate": lc.rate_ct_s.tolist(), "frames": lc.frame.tolist(), "members": rows}, indent=1))
    return rows

My ENLIL replica shows weaker agreement with CCMC ENLIL than expected (speed RMSE 93-135 km/s, density ratio 0.71-0.78). Before blaming model differences, I'll run a lagged correlation to check for a systematic timing offset.

Since the slices lack a pressure field, I'll infer ENLIL's pressure convention by fitting the Bernoulli constant along its fast-stream radials, using density, temperature, and velocity between 0.1 and 1 AU to test candidate conventions for p = f·(ρ/m_p)kT.

{
  "command": "~/miniconda3/envs/mhd_claude/bin/python -I -c "
import scipy.io as sio, numpy as np
f=sio.netcdf_file('ref/ccmc/raw/tim/tim.0220.nc','r',mmap=False)
r=f.variables['X1'][0]/1.495978707e11; D=f.variables['D'][1]; T=f.variables['T'][1]; V=f.variables['V1'][1]; V2=f.variables['V2'][1]; V3=f.variables['V3'][1]
mp=1.67262e-27; kB=1.380649e-23; GM=1.32712e20; AUm=1.495978707e11
i0=0; i1=np.argmin(abs(r-0.6))
v0=V[:,:,i0]
idx=np.argsort(v0.ravel())[-40:]
for fct in (1.0, 2.0, 2.15/1.2):
    res=[]
    for q in idx:
        k,j=np.unravel_index(q,v0.shape)
        if abs(V[k,j,:i1].max()-V[k,j,:i1].min())>0.25*V[k,j,0]: continue
        E=lambda i: 0.5*(V[k,j,i]**2+V2[k,j,i]**2+V3[k,j,i]**2)+2.5*fct*kB*T[k,j,i]/mp - GM/(r[i]*AUm)
        res.append((E(i1)-E(i0))/E(i0))
    print('f=%.2f'%fct, 'relative Bernoulli change 0.1->0.6 AU: median %.3f (n=%d)'%(np.median(res),len(res)))
print('r0',r[0],'T0 range',T[:,:,0].min(),T[:,:,0].max(),'v0 max',v0.max())
"",
  "description": "Fit ENLIL's pressure convention via Bernoulli"
}

Bernoulli isn't conserved along ENLIL's fast streams under any convention (-11% to -18% across 0.1–0.6 AU), pointing to extra energy terms via ENLIL's `q` parameter, with f=1 fitting best. I'll now test a replica variant with T scaled by 1.2/2.15 so thermal pressure matches ENLIL's directly.

It reconstructs n1=C/v^2 and T=D*v^2 after the speed offset, then applies existing density/temperature/magnetic/EMF scales. Existing ConeBoundary acts afterwards. The solver agent received the exact API and diff for a separate optional GPU derivative. This agent performed no GPU work, large simulation, or production source edit.

Existing constant-pressure/momentum claims apply only at vertices until an alternative closure is explicitly selected.
